before.title: 1.0 SCe Valve Cover Oil Leak Soaking Spark Plug Wells and Coils
before.description: The 1.0 SCe three-cylinder engine used in the Brazilian Sandero from the 2017 model year has a chronic oil leak at the plastic valve (tappet) cover. The cover's sealing degrades with heat cycles at low mileage — owners on Reclame Aqui describe it as a design defect — and oil seeps into the spark plug wells, soaking the spark plugs and the tips of the ignition coils. This causes misfires, rough running, and repeat fouling of new plugs and coils. Reclame Aqui complaints document leaks appearing on cars with as little as 20,000-30,000 km, sometimes recurring after dealer repair, and related seepage from the timing cover area on the side of the engine. Separately, Renault issued an official recall (service start September 2020) for 1.0-engined units produced July 2019 to January 2020 because a non-conforming oil feed orifice could starve the engine of lubrication, risking seizure or fire — affected owners should confirm completion at a dealer.
before.solution: Replace or reseal the valve cover with an updated gasket/sealant, clean the spark plug wells, and replace oil-fouled spark plugs and any saturated ignition coils. Inspect the timing cover joint at the same time, as it is a secondary leak point on the same engine. The job is inexpensive at an independent shop; the main cost driver is replacement coils if oil has damaged them. For 2020-build cars, check the official Renault recall portal (renault.com.br/recall) for the open oil-feed-orifice lubrication recall, which is repaired free of charge.
symptoms: Oil seepage visible around the valve cover edges
Oil pooled in the spark plug wells when plugs are removed
Engine misfire or rough idle
Oil-fouled spark plugs and oily ignition coil tips
Burning oil smell from the engine bay

before.title: 1.6 8V K7M Head Gasket Failure and Excessive Oil Consumption
before.description: Sanderos with the 1.6 8V K7M engine (the workhorse engine of the Brazilian lineup from launch in 2008 through the late 2010s) are widely reported by owners to consume engine oil at an abnormal rate, with the level dropping noticeably between changes and dark smoke from the exhaust. Brazilian repair sources and owner-complaint roundups (Mobiauto, Sua Oficina Online) attribute the recurring cases to a head gasket defect that lets oil pass into the combustion chambers, where it burns with the fuel mixture. Reclame Aqui complaints describe it as a chronic problem, with some owners told the engine was effectively disposable after repeated failures. External oil leaks at the head gasket joint and valve cover are also part of the pattern. Left unaddressed, sustained low oil level risks accelerated wear or engine failure.
before.solution: Check the oil level frequently — every fuel stop on affected cars — and investigate any consumption beyond roughly 0.5 L between services. Confirmed cases require head gasket replacement, with the head checked for flatness and resurfaced if needed; replace valve stem seals while the head is off if smoke persists. A head gasket job on the K7M is mechanically simple and affordable at Brazilian independent shops compared with dealers. Using the correct 10W-40/15W-40 viscosity specified for the K7M matters, since thinner oils worsen consumption on this engine.
symptoms: Oil level dropping rapidly between oil changes
Dark or bluish smoke from the exhaust
Burning oil smell after driving
Oil residue around the cylinder head gasket joint
Low oil warning on longer trips

before.title: Easy-R Automated Manual Gearbox Clutch and Actuator Failures
before.description: The ZF-supplied Easy-R 5-speed automated manual transmission, offered on Brazilian-market Sandero and Sandero Stepway 1.6 from 2014 production (model years 2015-2019), is one of the most complained-about Renault components on Reclame Aqui. Owners report shuddering and judder when pulling away from a stop appearing as early as 20,000-25,000 km, caused by premature clutch disc wear; failures of the clutch/gear actuator module that leave the car stuck in gear (frequently 2nd) or immobilized; harsh or delayed shifts; and isolated reports of dangerous behavior such as unintended reverse engagement and sudden downshifts at highway speed. Dealer repair quotes have reached R$15,000 (~USD 2,800), with the actuator module alone costing over R$4,400 as a genuine part. Renault discontinued the Easy-R gearbox in Brazil in 2019 after roughly five years on the market, and complaints continued well after the 3-year warranty expired. No recall was ever issued for the gearbox.
before.solution: There is no recall; repairs are owner-paid out of warranty. Premature judder requires replacement of the clutch kit (disc, pressure plate, release bearing) with the updated parts. Actuator faults require recalibration or replacement of the clutch/shift actuator module — independent transmission specialists in Brazil charge roughly half of dealer prices (around R$3,000 vs R$5,500+). After any clutch or actuator work, the system must be relearned/calibrated with a Renault-compatible scan tool (CLIP). Buyers of used 2015-2019 Sandero with Easy-R should test for takeoff shudder and hesitant engagement before purchase, and budget for actuator and clutch service life far shorter than a conventional manual.
symptoms: Shuddering or judder when pulling away from a stop
Jerky, delayed, or harsh gear changes
Gearbox stuck in a gear (often 2nd) or refusing to engage
Gearbox warning light or 'check gearbox' message on dash
Difficulty or delay engaging reverse
Vehicle immobilized with no gear engagement

before.title: Official Steering Safety Recalls: Ball Joints, Steering Box, and Hydraulic Hose
before.description: Renault Brazil has issued multiple official safety recalls on the Sandero for steering defects, all listed on the manufacturer's recall portal. In 2012, a batch of hydraulic steering boxes (chassis 93YJA1CJ840383-93YJA1CJ932550) had a manufacturing non-conformity that could cause steering malfunction or lock-up. In January 2016, 3,120 Sandero/Logan built November 4 - December 4, 2015 were recalled because non-conforming raw material in the axial ball joints (which connect the steering rack to the wheel ends) could cause the joint to break, resulting in loss of steering control. In November 2017, 13,026 Sandero, Logan, Duster, and Duster Oroch built July 29 - October 6, 2016 were recalled because the power steering low-pressure hose could rupture, leaking fluid and causing steering hardening or loss of assist. A related February 2017 recall covered suspension/steering fastening bolts on 2016-built cars torqued incorrectly, which could deform or break and alter steering behavior. All carry risk of accident with material damage and serious injury.
before.solution: Check whether a specific car is affected by entering the chassis number on Renault Brazil's recall page (renault.com.br/recall) or calling 0800 055 5615, and have any open recall performed free of charge at a Renault dealership — the ball joint inspection/replacement takes about 2.5 hours and the hose replacement about 90 minutes. Recall completion does not expire; used-car buyers should verify these campaigns were performed on 2012 and 2016-2017 model year cars before purchase. Any Sandero with steering play, stiffness, or fluid leaks at the rack should be inspected immediately regardless of recall status.
symptoms: Sudden steering stiffness or heavy steering effort
Power steering fluid leaking under the front of the car
Knocking or play in the steering over bumps
Whining or groaning from the steering pump as fluid is lost
Loss of steering control (ball joint rupture in extreme cases)

before.title: Steering Column Bearing Wear Causing Play and Knocking in the Steering Wheel
before.description: Sandero and its Logan twin suffer a chronic wear problem in the steering column's upper bearing. As the bearing wears, the steering wheel develops perceptible free play and a knocking or clunking sensation, felt especially over rough Brazilian pavement and during small corrections around center. Multiple independent Brazilian mechanic channels document the failure across both generations — including cars as recent as the 2020 Logan — and consistently call it a 'defeito crônico' of the platform. Dealers have been known to quote replacement of the complete steering column, but the documented root cause is just the column bearing, a cheap part. While mostly a nuisance, pronounced play degrades steering precision and several mechanics flag it as an accident risk if ignored long-term.
before.solution: Confirm the diagnosis by checking for free rotation play at the steering wheel with the front wheels held still — wear in the column bearing produces play and noise at the column itself rather than at the rack or tie rods (rule those out first, especially on cars covered by the steering recalls). Replace the steering column upper bearing; the part costs little and the job is a few hours' labor at an independent shop. Replacing the entire column assembly is unnecessary in the typical case and should only be needed if the shaft splines or tube are themselves damaged.
symptoms: Free play in the steering wheel before the wheels respond
Knocking or clunking felt in the steering wheel over bumps
Clicking or rattling noise from the steering column
Vague, imprecise steering around center
Noise when shaking the wheel with the car parked
